nonblocking.claim_broken: Round-1 OB-1b is CLOSED as specified (ack refused after reopen/release; only the claim holder's ack lands; killable on real PostgreSQL). Residual, new and narrow: the `claimed_by = worker_id` predicate is vacuous between two relay PROCESSES that both use the default id "relay" (nothing in D2 wires a per-process id; the round-2 drills use distinct ids 'relay'/'relay-b' that no code enforces). With the same id, B's late ack can land after A's pump re-claimed c and before A's enqueue; if A's enqueue then fails (capacity or any exception), `release_dispatch`/`fail_dispatch` are no-ops on an acknowledged row and c is delivered-but-unindexed until a rebuild.
nonblocking.evidence: Scratch drill test_r2_same_default_worker_id_late_ack_then_failed_enqueue (kept at the scratchpad path below), real PostgreSQL, plain AND Supabase images: B claims c as 'relay'; reopen(since); A re-claims c as 'relay'; B's ack -> 1 (landed); A's enqueue -> CapacityExhausted; release_dispatch -> 0; row (claimed, 'relay', acknowledged=True); after +30 s a fresh relay pump reads 0 rows for c; c in no index; printed 'STRANDED: c acknowledged, in no index, until a rebuild'. The same schedule with distinct ids (test_r2_exact_schedule_ack_after_reopen[relay-b]) refuses the ack (0). Also confirmed: with the DEFAULT id on both relays the exact round-1 schedule still passes (claimed_at predicate alone does that work) - the strand needs the failed enqueue in the instant after the late ack.
nonblocking.minimal_fix: One line: `worker_id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: f"relay-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}")` in OutboxRelay (unique per instance/process), and add to the Q3 delta that the Reconciler's relay id must be unique per process. Optionally a unit case asserting two default relays carry different ids.

nonblocking.claim_broken: New, SQL-surface only: `dispatch_pending` accepts a missing/NULL/blank worker_id (claim_preparation refuses one), so a row can be claimed with claimed_by NULL; under the new ack predicate NULL never equals anything, so nobody can ever acknowledge that row and it is redelivered every window forever (liveness churn, not a strand: the row stays pending). The shipped Python relay always passes a string, so no D2 path reaches it.
nonblocking.evidence: Scratch drill test_r2_sql_dispatch_pending_accepts_a_null_worker (plain + Supabase): dispatch_pending({limit, redelivery_s}) without worker_id claims c with (claimed_at set, claimed_by NULL); acknowledge_dispatch with worker_id NULL and with the key absent -> 0 and 0; +30 s -> the same row is handed out again, still (True, None, False).
nonblocking.minimal_fix: Mirror claim_preparation in dispatch_pending: `if p_args->>'worker_id' is null or length(btrim(p_args->>'worker_id')) = 0 then perform infrx.refuse('invalid_request', 'a worker id is required'); end if;`, one assertion in check_dispatch_details, one mutant (`if false then`).
